appearance_facts.fact: The line begins near the top of the plot in 2005 and descends steadily to the right, ending near the bottom in 2014. The 2005 and 2006 markers are at the same apparent height; the 2010 and 2011 markers are at nearly the same height; all other consecutive markers step downward.

appearance_facts.fact: The line spans from just above the 20 gridline (2005) to just above the 10 gridline (2014), covering roughly the upper half of the visible 0-to-20+ axis.
Each is lower than the previous, stepping down between the 20 and 15 gridlines, with 2009 sitting just below the 20 gridline.
Both sit just above the 15 gridline, with 2011 marginally lower than 2010.
2012 is just below the 15 gridline; 2013 is between the 10 and 15 gridlines, closer to 10.

Monotonically non-increasing across the decade, with the largest single-step drops appearing between 2006-2007 and 2008-2009; the total vertical drop from 2005 to 2014 is large relative to the axis span.

public_definitions: Goal: Review the river temperature dashboard for the 2005-2014 review period, determine whether the full-period change requires substantial-change follow-up, then submit the appropriate routing decision.
Comparison scope: full-period river temperature change, 2005 to 2014.
Routing criterion: Whether the full-period river temperature change requires substantial-change follow-up.

Options: (1) Route the 2005 to 2014 river temperature change to substantial-change follow-up; (2) Keep the 2005 to 2014 river temperature change on routine monitoring for ordinary variation; (3) Route the river temperature record to archive and background filing.
uncertain: No numeric threshold or rule defining 'substantial change' versus 'ordinary variation' is printed on the dashboard or in the policy tables.
No legend, series name, or station identifier is printed; the single line is unlabeled beyond the title.
The 2005 and 2006 labels both read 23.9°C, so the start-of-period value is unambiguous, but the exact magnitude of 'substantial' is not specified.
